                                                                                   M. August Rossi
                                                            Data Science Institute, University of Chicago, Chicago, IL, USA
                                                                                marossi@uchicago.edu



                                         Abstract. The metric distortion framework for analyzing single-winner ranked-choice voting rules
                                         assumes that voters and candidates occupy a shared metric space. Voting rules then attempt to elect
                                         a socially optimal candidate—one that minimizes the distance to all voters—using voters’ ordinal
                                         preferences alone. Voting rules that elect from the plurality veto core, a special case of the general




arXiv:2610.26535v1 [cs.GT] 19 Oct 2026

                                         vector p representing voter veto power and candidate weight vector q representing candidate support,
                                         contains all candidates with sufficient support to avoid being vetoed. SimultaneousPluralityVeto,
                                         the canonical method for electing from the plurality veto core, admits a significant flaw: it is not Pareto-
                                         efficient. Even though it intends to crown a single winner, there are elections for which it declares a
                                         tie bet

body_header:
COMPRESSION FORMULA FOR NONATTACKING FILLINGS OF
                                                    NON-SYMMETRIC MACDONALD POLYNOMIALS

                                                                                 ALEXANDER P. STEWART




                                                  Abstract. Macdonald polynomials are an important family of orthogonal polynomials




arXiv:2610.29950v1 [math.CO] 21 Oct 2026
                                                  that have applications to statistical physics. Corteel, Mandelshtam, and Williams proved a
                                                  combinatorial model involving multiline queues for partitions; however, their work does not
                                                  apply to weak compositions in general. We conjecture a first step towards this direction via
                                                  a variant of the nonattacking filling model for nonsymmetric Macdonald Polynomials Eµ .
                                                  This new model compresses the classical nonattacking filling model of Haglund, Haiman,
                                                  and Loehr and mirrors the concept of trivial pairs in the multiline queue model. We prove
                                                  it for a large family of weak compositions and explain the difficulty of extending this proof
                                                  to the general case.

                                           Keywords: Nonattacking Fillings, Multiline Queues, Macdonald Polynomials
                                           MSC classification: 05E05, 33D52
